svg.title: Extractly online evaluation with Human-in-the-Loop review
svg.desc: An application retrieves raw documents, calls Azure Content Understanding, and evaluates extracted values against source evidence without a Golden Dataset. Extractly uses schema checks, native Decision API field and structural evaluators, and optional application-supplied LLM or JEV evaluator adapters or AzureOpenAIGrader with the Foundry runner. An application-owned policy combines per-document review flags, configured score thresholds, coverage, errors, and business rules. Flagged extractions enter a human review queue for approval, correction, or rejection. Reports, reviewer decisions, corrections, and provenance are persisted for traceability. Evaluation scores are review signals, not calibrated accuracy probabilities or automatic approval.
svg.text: Use source evidence and explicit review signals to flag extracted documents before downstream processing
Do not treat CU confidence as proof
Supply one or combine as needed
Raw Documents to saved CU result
Retain Markdown, physical pages, and field spans
Pair predictions with the original analyzer schema
LLM / JEV / grader checks via evaluators=...
Decision checks use separately injected service clients.
LocalRunner does not make remote checks local.
Scores guide review; not calibrated accuracy
or approval probabilities. Checks are configurable.
Custom scores require application routing rules.
Report, source IDs, corrections, and decisions
Foundry: optional precomputed runner scores only
a future offline Golden Dataset, with approval.
Queue source document + extracted values + flagged fields
Include evidence, judgments, missing scope, and error context
Approve / correct / reject; inspect evidence side by side
Record reason, reviewer ID, and timestamp
Preserve the original prediction and evaluation for traceability
Continue downstream only when application policy permits
Keep human-verified status separate from model-only assessment
Human review and business approval are application-owned.
A passing aggregate gate never clears a document review flag.
Failure: hold and route for intervention
Reference-free evaluation is evidence-based, not proof of accuracy. Service errors, unsupported judgments, and incomplete coverage must never silently become approval.
